name: Corley's depot (the crossroads yard)
region: Lordaeron, below the sick village's ford; where the grain road crosses another road (a dirt junction with a leaning mile-post)

sensoryProfile.sight: A long shed with a weigh-house at one end, beaten-dirt yard, a green-rimmed water trough, a beam scale on a frame at the gate (iron pan swinging in no wind), three carts with shafts down, two cart horses tied at the rail of a lean-to office. Inside: a small iron stove with a kettle, one west window letting the afternoon sun across the counter and the ledgers on the back shelf, a wasp walking the glass.
sensoryProfile.sound: Kettle beginning to tick on the stove; the clerk's pen; Jaina's staff-heel knocking outside.
sensoryProfile.touch: Stifling hot in the office ('like standing in a boot'); cold comes in with Jaina like a draught.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: A small, ordinary, rule-bound place that turns out to be one spoke of a very large wheel.

establishedFacts.fact: The clerk is Corley: narrow, sleeve-guards, a cold, chewed pen, ink to the second knuckle. The yard master is in Andorhal until the end of the week; the books go down to Andorhal at the quarter and the master checks every line.
The out-book is a long sheepskin ledger ruled in faded red: day, carter, destination, sacks, beam weight, rate. Nearly every line has 'And.' in the margin (loads come in from Andorhal).

'Own cart' lines are free carters who buy in the yard and sell where they like; the yard is paid at the gate and records the load, not the man. Short-rate loads (two coppers under) began at midsummer: Millhaven first (twelve sacks, then again a fortnight on, then a third).
Counts by road, before the last month / since: north 9/3, west 7/4, south 11/6, east 1/9. 31 short-rate places in Corley's book; Corley knows where they all are.
Three loads of twenty sacks chalked on the scale for the day; carts in the yard held sixteen, seventeen and nineteen. Weights are taken on the carters' word and settled at Andorhal.
Sylvanas keeps the sheet (waybill paper, glazed) and Corley's copied list of the short-rate lines with dates.
A carters' inn stands across the road; the party sleeps in its loft (straw smelling of horses).

eventsHere.event: Sylvanas gets the out-book; Jaina reads the roads from the mile-post; the joint sheet is drawn; short-rate counts are made.
